key_insight: Severe plastic deformation increases both hardness and conductivity in CrMnFeCoNi, with thermal gains linked mainly to enhanced phonon transport rather than conventional defect-scattering behavior.
engineering_relevance: Defect and nanostructure engineering could enable high-entropy alloys that combine greater hardness with improved electrical and thermal transport.
method: Apply high-pressure torsion for up to four turns.
Characterize hierarchical defects and measure mechanical and transport properties.
Analyze electron and phonon contributions using Wiedemann–Franz and Cahill–Pohl models.
evidence_signal: After four turns, electrical conductivity rises from 0.953 to 1.003 ± 0.005 MS/m and thermal conductivity from 10.3 to 14.4 W/(m·K), while hardness saturates near 520 HV.
watch_item: Deformation-induced short-range ordering remains a proposed explanation, not an established mechanism for the conductivity increase.
paper_title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
